title: Store, session, identity and the commit
summary: store = .ObjectStore~new([language]); store~attach(name, engineOrFolder); s = store~session. s~find(cls, key) loads the object with all its parts (one object per key per session: a shared address is the same object for Tom and Rony); s~where(cls, attr, value); s~all(cls); s~new(cls) (unset values nil, many-parts empty arrays); s~delete(obj) (a NEW object becomes DROPPED); s~stateOf(obj) answers NEW, CLEAN, DELETED, DROPPED or ""; s~plan answers the statements a commit would run; s~commit runs them in one NoSQLServer transaction; s~rollback puts objects back as the database has them. store~map(cls) gives the ObjectMap (parts: ObjectPart with attribute, kind ONE|MANY|LINK, target, column, link, from, to, owned, targetClass).
procedure: A changed value is an UPDATE of that one column in its own table.
Keys first: new objects inserted after what they refer to, a child after its parent, link rows after both ends.
A delete: owned parts, link rows, extension rows, then the row itself; shared things stay.
Any refusal by the database rolls back the whole commit and says why.
invariants: Every object reached through a part must be in the session; a part holding a deleted object is refused.
Values are bound with DatabasePreparedStatement and DatabaseParameterBinder, typed from the catalogue (store~value): a phone stays text, a key a number, a quote is a quote.
Change a many-part by changing the array the object holds (append, delete); the session compares it with what it loaded.
